title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compares a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic validator. Under the frozen confirmatory semantics (shared_initial_candidate per pair) all confirmatory episodes completed: baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, seed_0) = 120/120 verifier passes. Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We (i) publish the full execution and analysis artifacts and SHA‑256 fingerprints needed to reproduce the run, (ii) use archived artifacts to diagnose why the paired outcome is uninformative about independent generative reliability (preregistered shared_initial_candidate design, template‑tight task synthesis, and validator–task coupling), and (iii) provide artifact‑grounded, runnable protocol modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed designs, validator diversity, expanded task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while answering operational questions about independent LLM reliability. The immutable initial master prompt is archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: Motivation. Translating high‑level operator intent into device configuration is a safety‑critical NetOps task: transient or final misconfigurations can break reachability, violate ACLs, or produce unsafe transient states. Deterministic offline validators (reachability/ACL/routing analyzers) provide auditable oracles for pre‑deployment correctness checks; coupling such verifiers to generative systems yields operationally meaningful automation. Research question and preregistered estimand. We preregistered CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 to answer a precise estimand: under frozen "shared_initial_candidate" semantics, does a single‑pass LLM generator (gpt‑5‑mini) produce verifier outcomes different from a deterministic template baseline? Concretely the primary estimand is the paired success‑rate difference (guarded minus baseline) across N = 120 paired tasks (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). This estimand tests verifier consistency across identical inputs, not independent generative reliability. Contribution. We (1) release a complete, byte‑for‑byte artifact bundle (responses, provider traces, per‑episode validator JSONs, execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256s) that reproduces the exact run; (2) report preregistered confirmatory results anchored to those artifacts (baseline = 120/120, guarded = 120/120; paired difference = 0.00; bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.0); and (3) provide artifact‑grounded, runnable protocol changes to answer the independent reliability question while preserving reproducibility.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded NetOps evaluation. Offline configuration analyzers (Batfish and related research) are standard tools for declarative, pre‑deployment verification of reachability, ACLs, and routing invariants; they provide deterministic, auditable checks of static device artifacts [Brown et al., 2023; doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Prior LLM→NetOps work commonly adopts generate–validate–repair pipelines; methodological axes that vary across studies include sampling semantics (single candidate vs independent per‑condition), repair budgets (single pass vs bounded K iterations), and validator scope (syntactic vs semantic vs multi‑verifier). Studies that measure independent generative reliability typically use independent per‑condition sampling or multi‑seed replication; those that focus on verifier behavior may intentionally reuse identical candidates. Our study intentionally preregistered the latter to test a distinct estimand (verifier response to identical inputs).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The full preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) fixed: N = 120 paired tasks (40 per topology class), confirmatory generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate", validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, primary estimator = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, analysis = paired_binary_analysis_v1 with 10,000 bootstrap resamples (seed = 1729). Task synthesis. Tasks were programmatically synthesized from deterministic templates (generator_id deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each manifest entry encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, per‑task workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), and difficulty annotations. These template constraints are enforced by the validator and are archived per task (execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json). Model and orchestration. The declared LLM was gpt‑5‑mini accessed through adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da...). Confirmatory generation semantics produced a single canonical candidate per task and reused it for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes (shared_initial_candidate files archived at execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt; representative SHA‑256s: task-000001 8f38c8be..., task-000002 ae967f70..., task-000003 f7f4db24...). Model‑call accounting and counting rule. The preregistered accounting counted one canonical generation per task when shared_initial semantics were used: planned_episode_count = 240 (120 pairs × 2 conditions) but model_calls_used = 120 because each pair used the same canonical generation for both scoring episodes. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 120 and completed_episode_count = 240 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Deterministic validator and scoring. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parsed commands, enforced per‑task workflow_policies and transient safety checks, computed final_state invariants, and emitted a structured JSON trace per episode (execution/scoring/*.json). The scoring rule for the confirmatory test required full_intent_constraint_validation (binary pass/fail). Contamination heuristics. Preregistered string‑overlap checks (exact match and normalized n‑gram overlap) were run and are recorded in analysis/contamination_summary.csv; no confirmatory items were flagged under the chosen thresholds, but the artifact bundle (provider call traces and canonical candidate hashes) is published to enable more exhaustive external audit.
sections.results: Confirmatory counts and exact inferential outputs (artifact grounded). All confirmatory episodes completed and are archived. Observed counts: complete_pair_count = 120; baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count (gpt‑5‑mini, shared_initial seed_0) = 120/120. The paired contingency table is n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). The preregistered primary estimator (mean of guarded_i − baseline_i) = 0.00. A 10,000‑resample percentile bootstrap (seed = 1729) produced a 95% CI [0.00, 0.00]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All per‑episode validator JSON traces that underlie these counts are published; representative examples are execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...), execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json (SHA‑256 993b8eb3...), and execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json (SHA‑256 dad1cf4c...). Diagnostic artifact evidence. Per‑episode traces show parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, and validation_after.valid = true for the canonical candidates (e.g., task‑000001 parsed_command_count = 4; required_command_count = 4). The degenerate paired outcome is explained directly by archived design choices: (i) shared_initial_candidate per pair (identical canonical file reused across both conditions; see execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt), and (ii) template‑tight tasks whose required_sequences are satisfied by template‑aligned canonical candidates. These two artifact‑visible facts make identical verifier outputs on both conditions the expected, correct result.
sections.discussion: What the confirmatory result legitimately shows—and does not show. The confirmatory statistics correctly evaluate the preregistered estimand: whether a deterministic validator produces different pass/fail outputs when presented with identical inputs under two scoring conditions. It does not estimate independent LLM generative reliability (the probability an independently sampled LLM candidate satisfies verifier constraints). Operationally relevant independent reliability requires independent_per_condition sampling or multi‑seed replication; the archived pipeline and artifacts support deterministic reruns under those semantics without creating new task definitions. Runnable, artifact‑grounded next steps. Using the published bundle a researcher can deterministically execute the following artifact‑grounded modifications: (A) independent_per_condition rerun: generate distinct seeds per condition per task (baseline seed_0, guarded seed_1), rescore with deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and recompute paired contrasts; (B) multi‑seed confirmatory design: draw K ≥ 3 independent seeds per condition per task to estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (C) validator diversification: add a second independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates to decouple validator–task coupling. All files required to run these protocols are present (execution/model_configuration.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/provider_calls/*, execution/responses/*). Threats to validity visible in the artifacts. Internal validity: shared_initial semantics intentionally removed sampling variance and therefore cannot measure independent generative variance. Construct validity: tightly templated tasks and a single deterministic validator can overstate success for template‑aligned candidates. External validity: a single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic tasks limit generalization. Conclusion validity: a degenerate contingency table yields trivial but correct inferential outputs; interpreting them beyond the precise estimand would be incorrect. We document these threats with per‑file traces and the full execution manifest so readers can deterministically reproduce and reframe the experiment.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and released an exhaustive artifact bundle to permit byte‑for‑byte replication. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both the deterministic template baseline and the gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition validated on all N = 120 tasks (both 120/120). Archived artifacts show that identical canonical candidates per pair and template‑tight task constraints caused the degenerate paired outcome; consequently the confirmatory paired result does not provide evidence about independent LLM generative reliability in production‑like sampling regimes. We provide artifact‑grounded runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversity) that transform the study into an informative independent generative reliability comparison while preserving reproducibility. All execution and analysis artifacts—including the immutable master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and the preregistration SHA‑256—are included to enable exact audit and follow‑up experiments.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
